evals.prompt: Build the self-review report for the partial-bundles branch. The findings and their saved runs are in scratch/findings.json.
evals.expected_output: A draft build, a visual check, a claims audit by a fresh subagent, then a final build tied to the audited data, opened for the user.
expectations: Writes the data with mode self and no feedback section
Builds a draft before any audit and fixes every build refusal in the data
Runs check_report.mjs and looks at the saved screenshots before the audit
Sends the audit brief to one fresh read-only subagent and repeats it after each fix until it passes
Builds the final page with --audit only after the audit passes on that exact data

evals.prompt: Build the report. One finding says the bug probably also affects refunds, but nothing ran or read the refund code.
evals.expected_output: The refund claim is cut, not listed as unknown or not checked.
expectations: Leaves the refund claim out of every field of the data
Does not add an unknowns or not-checked list
Does not mention dropped claims or the process on the page

evals.prompt: Build the self-review report for my uncommitted change in this checkout.
evals.expected_output: The head is a snapshot commit of the working tree, and the branch, index, and refs are left untouched.
expectations: Takes the head commit from scripts/snapshot.sh
Does not stage, commit, stash, or switch branches
Shows no GitHub links for the unpushed snapshot

evals.prompt: Build the report for PR 731. One flag's comment says the code breaks 'the resources standard', and another says 'the bundling guide' requires whole bundles.
evals.expected_output: Each source is named so a stranger knows what it is and linked: the coding standard by its page title and file, the guide by its page title and URL.
expectations: Replaces 'the resources standard' with the standard's page title, linked to its file at the commit read
Replaces 'the bundling guide' with the doc page's title, linked to its URL
Links the ticket, the PR description and code locations wherever a summary, comment or feedback body refers to them
Treats an unlinked or vaguely named source as an audit problem
